title: MESH render patches, version 1
description: What the MESH runtime's update produces (see docs/manual/runtime.md, "Update"): the operations that turn the previous render's tree into the new render's tree, when both come from one program. A renderer applies them in order. The law: applying them to the previous tree gives exactly the tree a full render of the new snapshot gives. A list is minimal in effect, not unique in form, so a renderer applies lists and never compares them. Nodes are named by their render-v1 keys, which the renderer compares only for equality. A prop or text a patch doesn't mention is unchanged. A change of structure (a node or text added, removed or reordered, a different component or event binding) is one `replace` of the whole tree: draw it afresh, reusing nothing. A `replace` is always the only operation of its list. This schema lists exactly the properties this MESH produces. A later MESH may add operations or properties without changing `version`, but a renderer that meets an operation it doesn't know must refuse the list, never skip it, since skipping would break the law; removing a property or changing a meaning is a new version.

key.description: A render-v1 key: a node's or text run's identity. Compare for equality only.

oneOf.description: The prop now has this value, and this MESH text if it has one (`propText`, as render-v1 carries it); a prop with no `propText` has none now.
The prop is now absent, with its text.
The tree is this one: draw it afresh, as for a program change, reusing nothing.
